- When sentiment is positive (≥0.5) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.25) and forecast is trending up, cap upward momentum at 1–2% above recent mean to prevent overshoot.  
- After a recent spike in price, model tends to overcorrect downward — adjust forecast to allow 1–3% lagged rebound before full correction.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (0.00) and forecast is consistently high, apply mean reversion bias: subtract 2–5% from forecasted values to align with historical volatility.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast to reflect recent mean reversion or sentiment-driven correction.  
- When sentiment spikes to 1.00, forecast should not exceed 10% above prior 7-day high — avoid “sentiment-driven inflation” in price.
